Q: What is the role of a router?
Option1: To forward data between different networks based on logical addresses
Option2: To broadcast all traffic to all ports

Q: What are common functions of a router?
Option1: Routing packets, connecting different networks, providing default gateway
Option2: Encrypting stored files, managing users, printing documents
Option3: Serving web pages, handling email, hosting databases
Option4: Testing cable performance, splicing fiber optic cables

Q: What is the role of a switch?
Option1: To connect devices within a network and forward traffic based on physical hardware addresses
Option3: To convert IP addresses to domain names

Q: What is the main difference between a router and a switch?
Option1: A router connects different networks, a switch connects devices within the same network
Option2: A router forwards frames, a switch forwards packets
Option3: A router is wireless, a switch is wired
Option4: A router is always virtual, a switch is always physical

Q: What is a firewall?
Option1: A device or software that monitors and filters network traffic based on security rules
Option4: A device that converts fiber to copper

Q: What is an intrusion detection system?
Option1: A system that monitors network traffic for suspicious activity and alerts administrators
Option3: A device that encrypts all traffic
Option4: A tool for assigning IP addresses

Q: What is an intrusion prevention system?
Option1: A system that monitors traffic and can actively block malicious activity
Option2: A system that only logs events
Option4: A type of wireless access point

Q: What is the main difference between IDS and IPS?
Option1: IDS alerts only, IPS can block traffic
Option2: IDS is physical, IPS is virtual
Option3: IDS works for wired, IPS for wireless
Option4: IDS uses encryption, IPS does not

Q: What is a load balancer?
Option1: A device that distributes traffic across multiple servers
Option2: A device that stores encryption keys
Option3: A tool for translating IP addresses

Q: What is a proxy?
Option1: A server that acts as an intermediary between clients and the internet

Q: What is network-attached storage?
Option1: A device that provides file-level storage over a network

Q: What is a storage area network?
Option1: A high-speed network providing block-level storage to servers
Option2: A device that stores media files

Q: What is the main difference between NAS and SAN?
Option1: NAS provides file-level access, SAN provides block-level access

Q: What is an access point?
Option1: A device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network

Q: What is a wireless controller?
Option1: A device that manages multiple wireless access points
Option2: A device for balancing network traffic

Q: What is a content delivery network?
Option1: A distributed system of servers delivering content based on user location

Q: What is a virtual private network?
Option1: A secure, encrypted connection over a public network
Option3: A tool for translating IP addresses

Q: What is quality of service?
Option1: A method of prioritizing certain types of network traffic
Option2: A system for encrypting cloud data
Option4: A process for assigning IP addresses

Q: What is time to live?
Option1: A value in a packet's header limiting how many hops it can take before being discarded
Option2: The maximum uptime of a device
Option4: The time to establish a connection

Q: Which two devices are most closely related to controlling incoming and outgoing traffic?
Option1: Firewall and intrusion prevention system

Q: Which two devices manage wireless connections?
Option1: Access point and wireless controller

Q: Which appliance would you use to store large shared files for multiple users?
Option1: Network-attached storage

Q: Which appliance would you use for high-speed block-level storage?
Option1: Storage area network

Q: Which function is most closely tied to securing remote connections?
Option1: Virtual private network

Q: In a scenario where a company wants faster website load times for global users, which solution is best?
Option1: Content delivery network

Q: Which function is most likely to limit the number of hops a packet can take?
Option1: Time to live

Q: What is the main difference between a firewall and an intrusion prevention system?
Option1: A firewall filters traffic based on rules, IPS can block malicious traffic in real-time
Option2: A firewall only works for wired networks, IPS works for wireless
Option3: A firewall encrypts traffic, IPS decrypts it
Option4: A firewall stores logs, IPS deletes them

Q: Which appliance is specifically designed to distribute network or application traffic evenly among servers?
Option1: Load balancer

Q: Which appliance sits between client devices and the internet to handle requests on their behalf?
Option1: Proxy

Q: In which situation would quality of service be most important?
Option1: When prioritizing voice and video traffic over other data to ensure call quality

Q: A company wants to share files between multiple departments with minimal setup cost. Which solution fits best?
Option1: Network-attached storage

Q: A company needs to host a database requiring high-speed block-level access. Which solution fits best?
Option1: Storage area network
